provenance: Hand-authored 2026-08-18 for M11 self-consistency evaluation (Document 47 Sec9.1). Synthetic figures, not real disclosed data.
claim: Operating margin improved primarily because of aggressive cost-cutting across the workforce.
evidence: Financial excerpt: Operating margin improved to 32.1% from 30.0%, entirely attributable to a one-time favorable tax settlement recorded in the quarter; headcount and operating expenses were flat year-over-year.
reference_rationale: The underlying fact (margin improved) is grounded, but the evidence explicitly attributes the improvement to a one-time tax settlement, not cost-cutting, and explicitly states headcount/opex were flat -- a causal contradiction, not just a numeric one.
